A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Community Forensics, with the same authors, dataset and research questions. The main text, Tables 1–4, Figures 1–14 and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original detector evaluations, diversity and robustness experiments, and appendix experiments on generator-type classification and training duration.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional detector comparisons in Table 2 and Figure 3. Its appendices also retain original empirical results.

M1.justification: The detector backbones, sigmoid classification head, end-to-end training and modified RandAugment procedure remain unchanged. The k-nearest-neighbor attribution procedure highlighted in the new Section 4.5 already appears in v1's Appendix A.

E1.justification: V2 adds RED140, described as 140K images from 140 generators, as an actually used training dataset for a comparator. Community Forensics, the evaluation benchmarks and the detection and attribution tasks remain unchanged. RED116 is discussed but explicitly not evaluated separately.

E2.justification: The comparison set expands substantially. Table 2 adds a high-resolution detector trained on RED140 using the authors' procedure; Figure 3 adds that detector, Aeroblade, LGrad and NPR. The existing Wang et al., Ojha et al. and GenImage comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds aggregate mean summaries in Table 2 and Figure 3. Table 1 also corrects GenImage's listed real-data source from 'Diffusion, GAN' to ImageNet. The new RED140 comparison uses the existing training procedure at 384 x 384; established splits and 52K/3K training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 5–7 revise evidence for the existing diversity, backbone, alignment and transformation analyses. In particular, manual-only training is now described as performing similarly to systematic-only training, rather than better. The analysis questions and appendix attribution and training-duration studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten model subsets with 100K images each for Figure 1 and four randomly sampled subsets for Figure 4, with means and standard errors. Figure 1's reporting details move from its caption to Section 4.3; this is not additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial comparator results in Table 2 and Figure 3 and revises existing comprehensive-set scores. For example, Ours–High res. changes from 0.991 mAP/92.5% accuracy to 0.987/89.2%; RED140 newly reports 0.764/56.2%. Figures 3 and 5–7 also change. Existing detectors' other Table 2 benchmark and public-set scores remain unchanged. The comprehensive-set revisions are not explained.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs. The operational generator categories and mathematical description of the augmentation procedure remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the claimed dataset-scale advantage from approximately 250 times prior collections to roughly 34 times the largest prior collection. The central contributions—Community Forensics, improved generalization through generator diversity, and effective standard classifiers—remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the semantic-alignment conclusion as applying with sufficiently large data. It interprets the manual subset's similar performance using fewer images as evidence of diversity's value, and expands the possible sources of diffusion-model diversity to include processing pipelines and architectural variations. The deployment limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents guidance-scale extraction and metadata sources in model cards and diffusers, and explains how the RED140 detector is trained. It removes v1's cited NSFW-filtering description; this establishes lost documentation, not that filtering actually stopped. Appendix training hyperparameters and dataset access information are retained.

R1.justification: A focused expansion acknowledges RED116 and RED140's larger generator collections, adds the three newly evaluated forensic methods, and cites two additional works concerning data bias and alignment. This refines the scale comparison and research context while retaining the positioning around community generators and diversity.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites and copyedits throughout the introduction, methods, captions and conclusion. Section 5 changes from 'Discussion' to 'Conclusion', and the existing appendix-application summary becomes Section 4.5. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two dataset rows; Table 2 gains a comparator row and mean columns. Figure 3 expands its bars and legend and adds a mean group, Figure 7 is restyled, and appendix displays are relocated. The overall figure set and document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The added detector comparisons and acknowledgment of RED116/RED140 strengthen the empirical comparison and make the scale claim more accurate. The qualified semantic-alignment conclusion also improves interpretation. These are useful, limited gains; unexplained comprehensive-set score revisions and removed filtering documentation leave reproducibility weaknesses.
